$comment: Release registry consumed by `cppgraph status` (update/rebuild advice) and by scripts/install.sh (default checkout target). `latest` is the newest STABLE version tag (null until the first release is cut → installers fall back to the main branch). Each `releases` entry: `version` (matches the git tag, with or without a leading 'v'), `rebuild` (which layer of the index stack adopting it invalidates: "none" = query-code only, the existing store stays valid; "store" = rebuild the SQLite store from the existing .scip, no recompile; "reindex" = re-run scip-clang then rebuild the store), optional one-line `notes`, and an optional `url` to that release's changelog (keep detail in the CHANGELOG/GitHub release, not here). Sort releases oldest->newest. Example entry: {"version": "0.1.0", "rebuild": "reindex", "notes": "reference index format changed", "url": "https://github.com/rakiz/cppgraph/releases/tag/v0.1.0"}.
$comment_scip_clang: `scip_clang` pins the indexer dependency by `version` (upstream scip-clang release tag; drives the download URL and the source clone in docker/build-scip-clang-patched-linux) plus `rebuild` (impact of adopting a DIFFERENT version, same vocabulary as releases: "reindex" in practice since a new indexer changes the .scip). `patchset_version` is independent of that upstream `version`: it pins THIS repo's own patch bundle applied on top of the tag (see $comment_patchset), and is stamped into a downloaded "patched" binary's scip-clang.json sidecar so `cppgraph status` can tell when the installed binary predates the current patchset. The *variant* (stock vs patched) is still a capability level, not a staleness axis: a graph's variant is independent of the locally installed binary (a patched-indexed graph can be copied to a stock-only machine), and `cppgraph status` reports the installed/graph variant for information, advising re-indexing only on a version change; what a graph actually carries (file vs symbol granularity) is surfaced via has_attributed_refs / the usage_view.
$comment_patchset: Patchset history — THIS repo's patch bundle on top of the pinned upstream tag, independent of `version`: 1 = enclosing_range (sourcegraph/scip-clang PR #504) only; 2 = + the ForwardDefinition declaration-site fix (scip-clang-patches/forward-definition-on-v0.4.0.patch); 3 = + the ReadAccess/WriteAccess syntactic classifier (scip-clang-patches/read-write-access-on-v0.4.0.patch); 4 = + the SymbolInformation.kind syntactic classifier (scip-clang-patches/kind-on-v0.4.0.patch); 5 = + SymbolInformation.signature_documentation for defined/pure-virtual functions & methods (scip-clang-patches/signature-documentation-on-v0.4.0.patch), which also widened forward-definition's addTo hunk to -U2 context (it could mis-land once enough lines shift above it — see that patch's header); 6 = + Relationship.is_type_definition for fields / file-scope variables / static data members (scip-clang-patches/typed-by-on-v0.4.0.patch), which also widened typed-by's emitDocumentOccurrencesAndSymbols hunk to -U2 context (its -U1 context also closes MacroIndexer's sibling function — see that patch's header). Bump it whenever a patch is added/removed/changed (NOT when upstream releases) — scripts/publish-scip-clang-patched.sh folds it into the release tag; see TODO.md's scip-clang section.

releases.notes: First release. No store/schema change — safe to update in place.

Store schema v4 across the release (`symbols.end_line` at v3 for `line_span`, `symbols.documentation` at v4 for `explain` doc comments), plus a dozen new read-only query commands (ranking/stats, `outline`/`class_members`, architecture facts like `boundary_violations`/`api_surface`/`dependency_cost`, `file:line` symbol resolution) and a generated CLI reference doc. v2/v3 stores keep working — the migration is store-level, no re-index: rebuild from the existing .scip (`cppgraph build`) to get the new columns; `update` migrates only files it actually touches, and `enrich-refs` migrates the schema shape without backfilling `end_line`/`documentation`.

Store schema v5 (`refs.roles`, `symbols.scip_kind`, `symbols.signature_documentation`, `symbols.is_out_of_project`) plus five new scip-clang syntactic-classifier patches on top of #504 (patchset 1→6): ForwardDefinition (fixes the declaration-site phantom-caller bug on stock-shaped graphs too), ReadAccess/WriteAccess (`--access {read,write}` on `references`/`find_references`), `SymbolInformation.kind` (`scip_kind` field), `signature_documentation` (signatures without a source read), and `Relationship.is_type_definition` (new `typed-by` edge kind: field/variable → its declared type, on `impact`/`reachable-from`/`boundary-violations`). Also consumes stock scip-clang's `Index.external_symbols` (`Node.is_out_of_project`, no patch needed — always-on, +~21% node count). v2–v4 stores keep working — store-level migration only, no re-index: rebuild from the existing `.scip` (`cppgraph build`) to get the new columns; `update`/`enrich-refs` migrate the schema shape without backfilling the new columns' data. Full detail in `CHANGELOG.md`.

Bugfixes only — no schema change (still v5), safe to update in place. Fixes a signature-attribution bug (a field could render a neighbouring function/operator's signature) and CLI/MCP crashing with a raw traceback instead of a clean error on a too-new store schema. Sharper hint on ambiguous name resolution (type vs. member vs. operator candidates). Plus regression tests closing gaps found in a migration-test audit (store schema, scip-clang binary staleness, scip.proto compatibility). Full detail in `CHANGELOG.md`.

No schema change (still v5), safe to update in place. CLI/MCP parity work (find gains --hide-trivial/--limit/--root and overload grouping; every hyphen/underscore subcommand now answers to both spellings) plus a full read-only codebase audit's findings: a real sweep-line attribution bug (co-starting nested definitions could misattribute a call/reference to the wrong enclosing symbol), stale docs (viz/README.md's missing path/cycle/boundary-violation modes, a resolved caller false-positive still described as open), dead code removed (Graph's unused in-memory query engine), a schema-compat perf anti-pattern replaced (get_node/find/references_of no longer probe legacy schemas via exception cascades), and a context-expansion filtering gap (--exclude-tests now reaches path/cycle mode's depth expansion). Full detail in `CHANGELOG.md`.
